answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers: in a forum called Onyx, each member locks a stake to join, then posts with a zero-knowledge proof of membership plus one share of its secret key tied to the epoch. One post per epoch reveals nothing; a second post leaks a second share, so anyone can rebuild the key and claim the stake. Ten identities posting ten times need ten stakes, so splitting saves nothing. Limits: a rich attacker can still buy many seats, and honest stakes sit on a ledge until a withdrawal delay ends, a long horizon for small agents.
